questions.q: In a hydraulic lift, the surface area of the input piston is \(6 \mathrm{~cm}^2\) and that of the output piston is \(1500 \mathrm{~cm}^2\). If 100 N force is applied to the input piston to raise the output piston by 20 cm, then the work done is _______ kJ.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{F}_1}{\mathrm{~A}_1}=\frac{\mathrm{F}_2}{\mathrm{~A}_2}, \frac{100}{6}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{1500}, \mathrm{~F}=\frac{50}{3} \times 1500 \\ & \mathrm{~F}=50 \times 500=25 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~N} \\ & \omega=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}} . \overrightarrow{\mathrm{S}}=25 \times 10^3 \times \frac{20}{100} \\ & =5 \times 10^3=5 \mathrm{~kJ}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The reading of pressure metre attached with a closed pipe is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. On opening the valve, water starts flowing and the reading of pressure metre falls to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The velocity of water is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>V</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> is _________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the change in pressure can be written as

P1-P2=12ρv2   ...1

From equation (1), it follows that

4.5×104-2.0×104=12×103×v2⇒2.5×104=12×103×v2⇒v2=50⇒v=50

Hence, V=50.

questions.q: There is an air bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> in a liquid of surface tension <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>075</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> at a depth of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> below the free surface. The amount by which the pressure inside the bubble is greater than the atmospheric pressure is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The pressure inside the bubble is given by 

ΔP=P-P0=ρgh+2Tr

The data given is 

r=10-3 mT=0.075 N m-1ρ=1000 kg m-3h=10 cm

Therefore, the pressure in the bubble is 

ΔP=1000×10×10×10-2+2×0.07510-3=1000+150=1150 Pa

questions.q: A small spherical ball of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> falls freely under gravity through a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> before entering a tank of water. If, after entering the water the velocity of ball does not change and it continue to fall with same constant velocity inside water, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> will be ____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, viscosity of water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>‐</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using equation of motion, v2=u2+2as

v2=0+2-g-h

⇒v2=2gh

Initial velocity of ball is v=2gh=20h.

 If after entering the water this velocity does not change, then this value should be equal to the terminal velocity.

Then, 2gh=29r2ρ-σgη, here, ρ is density of ball, σ is density of water and η is viscosity.

⇒20h=290.1×10-32104-103101×10-5⇒20h=2910-810-1103×101×10-5

⇒20h=400

∴h=20 m

questions.q: In a test experiment on a model aeroplane in wind tunnel, the flow speeds on the upper and lower surfaces of the wings are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>70</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>65</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively. If the wing area is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, the lift of the wing is _______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. (Given density of air <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's principle on upper & lower surfaces, we get

P1+12ρv12+ρgh1=P2+12ρv22+ρgh2

Since, height difference between upper and lower surface is negligible.

⇒P2-P1=12ρv12-12ρv22

Therefore, upthrust acting due to pressure difference:

⇒FA=12ρv12-v22⇒F=12×1.2×702-652×2

=810 N

questions.q: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>64</mn></math> identical drops each charged upto potential of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mV</mi></math> are combined to form a bigger drop. The potential of the bigger drop will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mV</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the potential V of each tiny drop is given by

V=kqr   ...1

When all the drops forms the bigger drop the radius of the new drop r' can be calculated as follows:

Volume of big drop=64×volume of each tiny drop⇒43πr'3=64×43πr3⇒r'=4r

So, the potential of the new big drop V' can be written as

V'=k64qr'=k64q4r=16kqr   ...2

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the potential of the new drop.

V'V=16kqrkqr⇒V'=16V   ...3

Substitute the value of the known parameter into equation (3) to calculate the required value of the potential for the new drop.

V'=16×10 mV=160 mV

questions.q: The diameter of an air bubble which was initially <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, rises steadily through a solution of density $1750 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ at the rate of $0.35 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Coefficient of viscosity of the solution is ______ (Assume mass of the bubble to be negligible) (Answer in Poise to the nearest integer)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the bubble is rising steadily the net force acting on it will be zero.

(Because of density of air is negligible, so the value of mg can be neglected)

So, the force of buoyancy B is equal to the weight of the displaced liquid acting upward is equal to the viscous force acting downward, i.e., B=F.

⇒4π3R3ρg=6πηRv

Putting R=1 mm=10-3 m, ρ=1.75×103 kg m-3, g=10 m s-2 and v=0.35×10-2 m s-1

η=109=1·11

In SI unit, η=11 poise CGS.

questions.q: A liquid of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>750</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> flows smoothly through a horizontal pipe that tapers in cross-sectional area from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. The pressure difference between the wide and narrow sections of the pipe is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi></math>. The rate of flow of liquid is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the equation of continuity, v2=2v1.

Applying the Bernoulli's Theorem,

P1+ρv122=P2+ρ4v122 ⇒P1-P2=3ρv122

⇒4500=3×750×v122  ⇒v1=2 m s-1

Now volume flow rate,Q=Av1=1.2×10-2×2=24×10-3 m3 s-1

questions.q: A metal block of base area 0.20 m2 is placed on a table, as shown in figure. A liquid film of thickness 0.25 mm is inserted between the block and the table. The block is pushed by a horizontal force of 0.1 N and moves with a constant speed. If the viscosity of the liquid is 5.0×10–3 Pl, the speed of block is ______ ×10-3 m s-1.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Viscous force is given by,

|F|=ηAΔvΔh

⇒0.1=5×10-3×0.2×v0.25×10-3

⇒v=0.025 m s-1

⇒v=25×10-3 m s-1

questions.q: A soap bubble of the radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is formed inside another soap bubble of radius, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The radius of an equivalent soap bubble that has the same excess pressure as inside the smaller bubble with respect to the atmospheric pressure is____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula of excess pressure inside the soap bubble is, 4TR here T is the surface tension and R is the radius of the soap bubble, 

⇒P0+4T6+4T3=P0+4TR

⇒16+13=1R⇒R=2 cm.

questions.q: The velocity of upper layer of water in a river is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Shearing stress between horizontal layers of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Depth of the river is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. (Co-efficient of viscosity of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The viscous force formula is given by,

F=-ηAdvdy

Therefore, shear stress FA=-ηdvdy. Here negative sign tells us that the direction of force is opposite to the velocity gradient.

⇒FA=ηdvdy

Now v=36×518=10 m s-1 and if the depth is d

dvdy=10d

⇒10-3=10-2×10d⇒d=100 m

questions.q: A big drop is formed by coalescing 1000 small droplets of water. The ratio of surface energy of 1000 droplets to that of energy of big drop is $\frac{10}{x}$. The value of $x$ is __________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} 1000 \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 & =\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \\ 10 r & =R \\ R & =10 r\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \frac{\text { S.E. of } 1000 \text { drops }}{\text { S.E. of Big drop }} & =\frac{1000\left(4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2\right) \mathrm{T}}{4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{~T}} \\ & =\frac{1000 \times \mathrm{r}^2}{(10 \mathrm{r})^2}=10=\frac{10}{\mathrm{x}} \\ \therefore \quad x & =1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Small water droplets of radius $0.01 \mathrm{~mm}$ are formed in the upper atmosphere and falling with a terminal velocity of $10 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Due to condensation, if 8 such droplets are coalesced and formed a larger drop, the new terminal velocity will be _____$\mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{m}=$ mass of small drop
$\mathrm{M}=$ mass of bigger drop
$\begin{aligned} & V_t=\frac{2}{9} \frac{R^2(\rho-\sigma) g}{\eta} \\ & 8 \propto m=M \\ & 8 r^3=R^3 \Rightarrow R=2 R\end{aligned}$
as $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{t}} \times \mathrm{R}^2 \quad \because$ Radius double so $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{t}}$ becomes 4 time
$\therefore 4 \times 10=40 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.q: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble A in air is half the excess pressure inside another soap bubble B in air. If the volume of the bubble A is $n$ times the volume of the bubble $B$, then, the value of $n$ is ___.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{P}=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\Delta \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}}=2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}}\right)^3=8\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An air bubble of diameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> rises steadily through a solution of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1750</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> at the rate of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>35</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The co-efficient of viscosity of the solution (neglect density of air) is ________ Pas (given, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The bubble is moving with a constant velocity so the net force acting on the body is zero.

Stokes' law defines the drag force which is given by F=6πηrv

The buoyant force is given by B=Vρg=43πr3ρg

Hence, it can be written that

43πr3ρg=6πηrv⇒η=2r2ρg9v=2×3×10-32×1750×109×0.35×10-2=10 Pas

questions.q: A soap bubble is blown to a diameter of $7 \mathrm{~cm} .36960 \mathrm{erg}$ of work is done in blowing it further. If surface tension of soap solution is $40 \mathrm{dyne} / \mathrm{cm}$ then the new radius is______ $\mathrm{cm}$ Take $\left(\pi=\frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \omega=\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{S} \Delta \mathrm{A} \\ & 36960 \mathrm{erg}=\frac{40 \text { dyne }}{\mathrm{cm}} 8 \pi\left[(\mathrm{r})^2-\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2\right] \mathrm{cm}^2 \\ & \mathrm{r}=7 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Suppose you have taken a dilute solution of oleic acid in such a way that its concentration becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></math> of oleic acid per <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> of the solution. Then you make a thin film of this solution (monomolecular thickness) of area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> by considering <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn></math> spherical drops of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mrow><mn>40</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac></mfenced><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Then the thickness of oleic acid layer will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. Where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ________ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
4tT=100×43πr3

=100×4π3×340π×10-9=10-8 cm3

tT=25×10-10 cm=25×10-12 m

t0=0.01tT=25×10-14 m⇒x=25.

questions.q: A spherical drop of liquid splits into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn></math> identical spherical drops. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math> is the surface energy of the original drop and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></math> is the total surface energy of the resulting drops, the (ignoring evaporation), <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi mathvariant="italic">u</mi><mi mathvariant="italic">f</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="italic">u</mi><mi mathvariant="italic">i</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mfenced></math>. Then value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let R be the radius of bigger drop and r be the radius of smaller drop.

Here, volume will remain conserved, so VR=Vr.

⇒43πR3=1000×43πr3

⇒R=10r

As surface energy is stated as u=SA, here, S is surface tension and A is surface area.

Thus, ui=S4πR2 and uf=S4πr2×1000

The ratio is ufui=1000r2R2

⇒ufui=101

Hence, the value of x=1.

questions.q: An air bubble of radius 1.0 mm is observed at a depth of 20 cm below the free surface of a liquid having surface tension $0.095 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{m}^2$ and density $10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. The difference between pressure inside the bubble and atmospheric pressure is _____ $\mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^2$. (Take $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\Delta \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{in}}-\mathrm{P}_0\begin{aligned} & =\rho \mathrm{gh}+\frac{2 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{1000 \times 10 \times 20}{100}+\frac{2 \times 0.095}{10^{-3}} \\ & =2000+190 \\ & =2190\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The surface tension of soap solution is  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The amount of work done required to increase the radius of soap bubble from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math> . (take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>22</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The amount of work done is equal to the change in the surface energy to increase the radius of the bubble.

The formula to calculate the change in surface energy is given by

 ΔU=2(T×ΔA)   ...1

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required work done.

∆U=3.5×10-2×4π(0.2)2-(0.1)2×2 J=3.5×10-2×4×227×0.03×2=2×1.32×10-2=264×10-4 J
